HMW-V18: Fleet Dispatch Availability

"How might we help FM dispatchers know which drivers and vehicles are free — without leaving the Fleet page to check active jobs?"
Context (TODO-047 extension): The Fleet page (implemented) shows drivers and vehicles as a pure master-data CRUD table. The Active/Inactive status tells whether a driver is theoretically available, not whether they're currently executing a job. Dispatchers at HaleSun manage 10-15 FM jobs/day with 8 drivers. When a new pickup arrives, they need to answer "who can I assign?" in seconds — not by cross-referencing My Jobs. The design question: should Fleet be operational-aware (show current job context) or remain a pure admin view?
Related implementation gap (DESIGN-AUDIT FINDING-04): JobDetailPage.tsx currently loads drivers from seedDrivers (hardcoded mock data) instead of the Fleet page's localStorage-backed fleet data. Drivers added in Fleet don't appear in job assignment dropdowns. This must be fixed regardless of which option is chosen — it's a data-plumbing fix, not a design choice.

Option A — Current: Pure CRUD table (implemented)

Status: Implemented
Drivers and vehicles are master data. Fleet is an admin screen, not a dispatch board. Active/Inactive is the only status that matters here; job assignment state belongs in My Jobs. Simplest; zero new data dependencies; works even when job context isn't loaded.

Pros
• Clean single-concern screen (just fleet data)
• No dependency on trip context state
• Already implemented and working
• Easy to reason about — status is simple boolean
Cons
• Dispatcher must open My Jobs to check who's available
• Cannot distinguish "Active but on a job" from "Active and free"
• Cognitive switch cost when dispatch decisions are time-sensitive
• 3 screen navigations to dispatch a new job (Jobs → Fleet → Jobs)

Option B — Dispatch-aware: Availability column (recommended)

Recommended
Add a computed Availability column to the Drivers table. When a driver is assigned to an active (Pending or In Progress) job, show the job reference with a faint blue dot. When unassigned, show green "Available." The column is derived from the shared trip context — no new API calls, no new data model changes. Dispatchers see who's free at a glance without leaving Fleet.

Pros
• Dispatcher answers "who's free?" in one screen
• Derived from existing trip context — zero new data model
• Job reference links to job detail for context
• Column only appears when meaningful (can hide for non-FM vendors)
• Color discipline maintained: green = available (same as Verified green), blue dot = in-progress (same as job status)
Cons
• Requires loading trip context on Fleet page (currently stateless)
• "Availability" derived from current assignments, not real GPS — may be stale if job runs over schedule
• Adds column width pressure at 768px (7 cols total for drivers)
• "Dispatched (Pending)" vs "On job (In Progress)" distinction may confuse operators
Color rules for Availability column: Green dot + "Available" uses #059669 (Verified green) — correct: this is an operational "clear" signal, not status. Blue dot + "On job" uses #152CFF (In Progress dot) — same signal the driver's job shows on My Jobs. Ghost + "Dispatched" uses #d1d5db + #6b7280 — Pending state. No new colors introduced. Color budget per row = 1 accent (either blue for on-job OR green for available — never both).

Option C — Dispatch Board: Visual availability panel (rejected)

Rejected — cards violate design system
A dedicated "Today's Dispatch" panel above the table shows driver cards with availability badges — at-a-glance who's free, who's on a job, with job location shown. This is the pattern used in many logistics dispatch tools.

Pros
• Very fast visual scan at glance
• Cards can show route summary ("Shenzhen → GZ")
• Familiar UX pattern for dispatch tools
Cons — WHY REJECTED
• Cards violate the design system — "tables not cards"
• Creates a duplicate view: board + CRUD table redundantly show same drivers
• Card grid breaks at 768px (3-col collapses to 1-col = wasted space)
• Adds a second concern to the Fleet page (was: admin data; now: operational dispatch)
• "AI slop" pattern — exactly the bubbly dashboard look the design system rejects

Option B — Tablet adaptation (768px)

At 768px, 7 columns is tight. Drop WeChat ID column; stack driver name + phone into one cell. Availability and Status columns remain visible — these are the two operational signals that matter most for dispatch decisions.

Verdict: Option B — Dispatch-aware availability column

Implement Option B as a v1.1 enhancement to the existing Fleet page. The Availability column answers the dispatcher's primary question ("who's free?") without changing the page's CRUD purpose or introducing cards. It uses only existing color tokens, is derivable from the shared TripContext, and degrades gracefully (hidden for inactive drivers; shows "—" if no trip context).

Implementation note — fix data plumbing first: Before adding Availability, resolve the data sync gap: JobDetailPage.tsx must load drivers/vehicles from localStorage (Fleet page's store) rather than seedDrivers/seedVehicles. Option B is only useful when the data pipeline is end-to-end. This fix is a prerequisite.

Phasing:
v1.0 — Current (Option A): Inline CRUD, Active/Inactive ✅ Done
v1.1 — Option B: Add Availability column + fix data plumbing (no design risk)
v2.0 — Consider: click on job ref in Availability column → deep-link to job detail on My Jobs

Open question: Should "Dispatched (Pending)" and "On job (In Progress)" be treated as one "Busy" state in the Availability column, or kept distinct? The distinction matters for multi-job vendors (a driver dispatched on J07 but not yet started could theoretically be reassigned). Recommend keeping them distinct (as shown in Option B) to match the same Pending/In-Progress semantics used everywhere else.
